root_cause.text: In KVM x86 LAPIC periodic timer handling, `advance_periodic_target_expiration()` blindly advanced `apic->lapic_timer.target_expiration` by one period even when the previous deadline was already in the past after vCPU inactivity, causing repeated expired reprogramming and a negative `delta` that could overflow the VMX preemption timer path.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a `ktime_before(..., now)` check in `arch/x86/kvm/lapic.c` to clamp `target_expiration` to `now`, with comments explicitly stating that past expirations after prolonged VM توقف lead to “waste host cycles,” “hard lockup,” and that keeping expiration in the past makes `delta` negative and can make `tscdeadline` “excessively large”; the CVE description says blindly adding the period can generate an unbounded number of hrtimer IRQs and hard lockups, especially with Intel HV timer.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clamp periodic LAPIC timer expirations to the current time to prevent catch-up loops and invalid TSC deadline calculations after long VM pauses.
intent_record.what: The function `advance_periodic_target_expiration()` keeps incrementing `apic->lapic_timer.target_expiration` by `apic->lapic_timer.period` as before, but now adds a check that clamps `target_expiration` to `now` if the computed expiration is earlier than the current time. It also adds comments explaining the synchronization rationale and the new past-expiration handling before computing `delta` and updating `tscdeadline`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, if the periodic timer's next expiration would fall in the past, the code now advances it to the current time instead of leaving it behind. This prevents KVM from attempting to catch up on missed periodic events, avoids useless repeated restart behavior, and ensures the computed `delta` stays non-negative so the TSC deadline does not become incorrectly large due to unsigned underflow.

grouping_result.intent: Clamp periodic LAPIC timer expirations to the current time to prevent catch-up loops and invalid TSC deadline calculations after long VM pauses.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the same LAPIC periodic timer bug: it clamps periodic expirations to current time to avoid advancing an already-expired deadline and prevents negative/overflowing deadline calculations after vCPU inactivity.

candidates.rationale: This is the statement that unconditionally advances the periodic timer deadline before checking whether the previous expiration is already stale, which is the root cause of the catch-up loop and negative delta behavior.
This call blindly adds one period to the old target_expiration even when it is already in the past after VM inactivity, directly causing repeated expired reprogramming and an invalid negative delta.
This computes the delta from a potentially stale target_expiration; when the deadline is behind now, the result becomes negative and can feed the problematic VMX preemption timer path.
This uses the computed delta to program the TSC deadline; once delta becomes negative due to the stale periodic expiration, this path can overflow or misprogram the timer.

This uses the computed delta to program the TSC deadline, so a negative delta caused by the stale periodic expiration can overflow or misprogram the timer.

    KVM: LAPIC: add APIC Timer periodic/oneshot mode VMX preemption timer support
    
    Most windows guests still utilize APIC Timer periodic/oneshot mode
    instead of tsc-deadline mode, and the APIC Timer periodic/oneshot
    mode are still emulated by high overhead hrtimer on host. This patch
    converts the expected expire time of the periodic/oneshot mode
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function bodies already contain the relevant fix logic, not the vulnerable construct. The root cause was that periodic handling would "blindly advanced apic->lapic_timer.target_expiration by one period even when the previous deadline was already in the past". In this diff, `advance_periodic_target_expiration()` only does the period advance (`apic->lapic_timer.target_expiration = ktime_add_ns(...)`), but the code now checks for overdue one-shot/periodic state before starting software timers: `if (apic_lvtt_oneshot(apic) && ktime_after(..., apic->lapic_timer.target_expiration)) { apic_timer_expired(apic); return; }`. Also `start_apic_timer()` now initializes `target_expiration` via `set_target_expiration(apic)`, and `kvm_lapic_expired_hv_timer()` advances only after expiry handling, then restarts via `start_hv_timer()` or `start_sw_period()`. There is no sign here of the old buggy behavior of reprogramming with a stale past deadline without checking it first.

    x86/kvm: fix LAPIC timer drift when guest uses periodic mode
    
    Since 4.10, commit 8003c9ae204e (KVM: LAPIC: add APIC Timer
    periodic/oneshot mode VMX preemption timer support), guests using
    periodic LAPIC timers (such as FreeBSD 8.4) would see their timers
    drift significantly over time.
    
    Differences in the underlying clocks and nume
bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function already contains the synchronization fix and does not blindly advance only the TSC deadline. Instead of just doing `apic->lapic_timer.tscdeadline += nsec_to_cycles(...)`, it now updates `target_expiration` using `ktime_add_ns(...)` and then recomputes `tscdeadline` from a common time source: `ktime_t now = ktime_get();`, `delta = ktime_sub(apic->lapic_timer.target_expiration, now);`, and `apic->lapic_timer.tscdeadline = kvm_read_l1_tsc(apic->vcpu, tscl) + nsec_to_cycles(apic->vcpu, delta);`. This is the fix described in the commit message: synchronizing both deadlines to the same time source on every tick to prevent drift and avoiding the buggy behavior where the deadline is advanced independently and can accumulate error. Therefore the vulnerable construct is not present in this version, and the fix is already present.
